text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair on Wednesday outlined the deal he had struck with European Union leaders about fishing and quota-hopping.
Blair told parliament that boats flying the British flag would have to land half their catch in British ports and said the EU had toughened up controls for fishermen who ignored the new rules.

"We secured an agreement with the Commission. Economic benefits from boats flying the British flag should go to British ports, for example through a proviso that 50 percent of the boats' catch should be landed locally," he said.
Britain would introduce new licence conditions to reflect that.
He said the Commission also agreed that new, tougher enforcement measures would be brought forward to tackle fishermen who insist on landing their catch abroad.
"These measures were agreed by qualified majority voting and therefore cannot be blocked by another member state," he said.

Quota-hopping refers to the legal practice whereby foreign, mainly Spanish, fishermen have bought up about a quarter of the British fishing fleet and their licences to allow them to fish in British waters.
"These agreements, taken together, will mean a major disincentive to quota-hoppers, present and future," Blair said.
